properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.3 is a transitive dependency of elliptic (which ethers uses) declared in both package-lock.json trees. It ships the SHA-1/SHA-2 family to this build; no direct application call site found — presence is what the inventory records. Same library as LIB-e966a74e (frontend lockfile entry).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the transaction-signing curve of the whole repository: the hardhat deployer account (hardhat.config.js:7, ethers.Wallet.createRandom) and the week_02 dApp (MetaMask + ethers) both sign ECDSA-secp256k1. Quantum-unsafe under Shor, but replacement needs an Ethereum protocol-level change — observable here, not fixable unilaterally in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the legacy OpenSSL single-round MD5 KDF ships inside the frontend bundle's browser crypto shim; the application itself never derives keys from passwords. Recorded as shipped-library surface (retroactive risk applies only if the shim is ever used).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 0.14.5 in the root lockfile provides Ed25519 signatures (plus X25519 ECDH and XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD) to the Ethereum JS toolchain — pulled in by bcrypt-pbkdf and wallet libraries. The build ships Ed25519; no first-party signing call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory in the week_02 frontend: elliptic is the secp256k1 implementation underneath ethers.js, and the dApp (pages/index.js) drives ECDSA signatures through the MetaMask/ethers signer. Same library as LIB-a0bfbc1a.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: X25519 key agreement is available in the shipped library via tweetnacl; no application call site found. Recorded as shipped-library surface; migration to hybrid X25519+ML-KEM would be at whatever code eventually uses it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory plus app-level use: keccak256 (pre-FIPS SHA-3 padding) is Ethereum's core hash, and the Solidity code in this repo uses it directly (RandomNumbers.sol:7, the sample_apps/11_flash_loan ERC-3156 magic values). The lockfile entries document the runtime side of the same primitive.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 key derivation ships with this repo's Ethereum toolchain via three declared packages seen across all 29 sites in both lockfiles (root and week_02 frontend): @ethersproject/pbkdf2 5.7.0 (ethers mnemonic/key derivation), the pbkdf2 npm package ^3.x (browserify polyfill), and @types/pbkdf2 (type stubs documenting the dependency surface). Declared dependency = the build ships the KDF; no first-party PBKDF2 call site found in the application's contracts or scripts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-js is the KDF for Ethereum JSON keystores (used by ethers' keystore functions); the app never creates keystores directly, but the KDF ships with the ethers dependency tree. Memory-hard, symmetric — not a PQ migration concern.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl's secretbox AEAD; no application call site found. Symmetric AEAD with 256-bit keys — Grover only halves it to 128-bit, so it is not urgent, but it belongs in the inventory as shipped-library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 0.14.5 is declared as a dependency (root package-lock.json; pulled in via bcrypt-pbkdf and wallet libraries). The shipped build carries tweetnacl's full classical suite: Ed25519 signatures, X25519 ECDH, XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD and SHA-512 — all quantum-unsafe. No first-party call site found in application code; available to any installed code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.1.1 is declared in the root lockfile (dependency of the ethers/ethereum-cryptography toolchain) and ships SHA-256, SHA-3/Keccak, BLAKE3 and more. Library-level provider entry for the separately recorded SHA-256/BLAKE3/SHA-3 primitive objects; no application call site found, but the hashes are available to any installed code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-js is the Ethereum keystore KDF; this is the frontend's copy (the tree also carries scrypt-js@3.0.1 under a different parent, covered by ALG-c1f8b585). No application call site, but it ships with the bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js 2.4.11 (pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 streamable implementation) declared in the root lockfile as a transitive dependency. The build ships these hash implementations; SHA-1 among them is broken for collision resistance. No first-party call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic is the secp256k1 ECDSA implementation beneath ethers.js/MetaMask signing; the frontend's transaction-signing path (pages/index.js getSigner → buyCoffee) depends on it. Quantum-unsafe under Shor; replaceable only ecosystem-wide. Same library facet as ALG-710f61f0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js ships SHA-1/SHA-2 to the frontend build as a transitive dep of elliptic; no direct application call site. Same library facet as ALG-50e53f84 (the algorithm-level object).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 3.1.2 (browser-compatible PBKDF2) declared in the root lockfile as a transitive dependency of the web3 toolchain. Ships the PBKDF2 KDF to any installed code; no first-party call site found in application code.
